metadata.title: Geometry of $CRS$ bi-warped product submanifolds in Sasakian and cosymplectic manifolds

nodes.name: Bi-warped product
nodes.statement: Let $B,N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ be Riemannian manifolds equipped with metrics $g_B,g_1$ and $g_{2}$, respectively, and let $f_{1},f_{2}$ be two positive functions on $B$. Then the {\it bi-warped product} $B\times_{f_{1}} N_{1}\times_{f_{2}} N_{2}$ is the product manifold $B\times N_{1}\times N_{2}$ equipped with the bi-warped product metric \begin{equation} g=g_B+f_{1}^2 g_1+f_{2}^2 g_2.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The product $B\times N_1\times N_2$ carrying the metric $g=g_B+f_1^2g_1+f_2^2g_2$ for positive warping functions $f_1,f_2$ on $B$.
differentia: equipped with the bi-warped product metric $g=g_B+f_{1}^2 g_1+f_{2}^2 g_2$

nodes.name: $CR$ submanifold
nodes.statement: A submanifold $M$ of a Kaehler manifold $(\widetilde M, \widetilde g,J)$ is called a {\it $CR$ submanifold} \cite{bejancu} if there exist a holomorphic distribution $\mathfrak D^{T}$ and a totally real distribution $\mathfrak D^\perp$ on $M$ such that $TM=\mathfrak D^{T}\oplus \mathfrak D^\perp$, where $TM$ denotes the tangent bundle of $M$.
nodes.genus: submanifold $M$ of a Kaehler manifold $(\widetilde M, \widetilde g,J)$
differentia: there exist a holomorphic distribution $\mathfrak D^{T}$ and a totally real distribution $\mathfrak D^\perp$ on $M$ such that $TM=\mathfrak D^{T}\oplus \mathfrak D^\perp$

nodes.name: $CR$-warped products
nodes.statement: He simply called such warped product submanifolds $N_{T}\times_f N^{n_{1}}_{\perp}$ to be {\it $CR$-warped products}.

nodes.name: Contact metric manifold
nodes.statement: A $(2m+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(\widetilde M^{2m+1}, g)$ is said to be a {\it{contact metric manifold}} if it admits a $(1, 1)$ tensor field $\varphi$ on its tangent bundle $T\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, a vector field ${\mathfrak{\xi}}$ (i.e., the structure vector field) and a $1$-form $\eta$ satisfying: \begin{equation}\begin{aligned} &\varphi^2=-Id+\eta\otimes{\mathfrak{\xi}},\,\,\,\eta({\mathfrak{\xi}})=1,\,\,\,\varphi(\xi)=0,\,\,\,\eta\circ\varphi=0,\\ &g(\varphi X, \varphi Y)=g(X, Y)-\eta(X)\eta(Y),\,\,\,\eta(X)=g(X, {\mathfrak{\xi}}). \end{aligned}\end{equation} for any vector fields $X, Y$ on $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, where $\widetilde\nabla$ denotes the Riemannian connection with respect to the Riemannian metric $g$ (see \cite{Bl}).
nodes.statement_short: An odd-dimensional Riemannian manifold carrying a compatible structure $(\varphi,\xi,\eta,g)$ satisfying the standard contact metric identities.
differentia: it admits a $(1, 1)$ tensor field $\varphi$ on its tangent bundle $T\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, a vector field ${\mathfrak{\xi}}$ (i.e., the structure vector field) and a $1$-form $\eta$

nodes.name: Normal almost contact metric manifold
nodes.statement: An almost contact metric manifold $(\widetilde M, g, \varphi, \xi, \eta)$ is said to be {\textit{normal}} if the tensor field $N_{\varphi}=[\varphi, \varphi]+2d\eta\otimes\xi$ vanishes identically, where $[\varphi, \varphi]$ denotes the Nijenhuis tensor of $\varphi$.
nodes.genus: almost contact metric manifold $(\widetilde M, g, \varphi, \xi, \eta)$

nodes.name: Sasakian manifold
nodes.statement: A normal contact metric manifold is said to be a {\textit{Sasakian manifold}}.

nodes.name: Almost cosymplectic manifold
nodes.statement: An almost contact metric manifold is called {\em{almost cosymplectic}} if $d\eta=0$ and $d\varphi=0$ according to D. E. Blair in \cite{Bl}.

nodes.name: Cosymplectic manifold
nodes.statement: In particular, an almost cosymplectic manifold is called {\em{cosymplectic}} if it satisfies \begin{align} \widetilde\nabla\varphi=0,\quad \widetilde\nabla\xi=0. \end{align}

nodes.name: Mean curvature vector $H$
nodes.statement: The mean curvature vector $H$ is defined by $H=\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} h(e_i, e_i)$.
nodes.genus: normal vector field of the submanifold

nodes.name: Totally geodesic, totally umbilical and minimal submanifolds
nodes.statement: A submanifold $M$ is called {\it totally geodesic} if $h=0$; {\it totally umbilical} if $h(X, Y)=g(X, Y)H$; and {\it minimal} if $H=0$.

nodes.name: Invariant submanifold
nodes.statement: A submanifold $M^{2n+1}$ tangent to ${\mathfrak{\xi}}$ is called {\textit{invariant}} if $\varphi$ preserves each tangent space of $M^{2n+1}$, i.e., $\varphi(T_xM^{2n+1})\subseteq T_xM^{2n+1}, \forall x\in M^{2n+1}$.
differentia: $\varphi$ preserves each tangent space of $M^{2n+1}$, i.e., $\varphi(T_xM^{2n+1})\subseteq T_xM^{2n+1}, \forall x\in M^{2n+1}$

nodes.name: Anti-invariant submanifold
nodes.statement: A submanifold $M^{n}$ is called {\textit{anti-invariant}} if $\varphi$ maps any tangent space of $M^{n}$ into the corresponding normal space, i.e., $\varphi(T_xM^{n})\subset T^\perp_xM^{n}, \forall x\in M^{n}$.
differentia: $\varphi$ maps any tangent space of $M^{n}$ into the corresponding normal space, i.e., $\varphi(T_xM^{n})\subset T^\perp_xM^{n}, \forall x\in M^{n}$

nodes.name: Pointwise slant submanifold and slant function
nodes.statement: A submanifold $M^{n}$ is called {\textit{pointwise slant}} \cite{Etayo,CG} if for any nonzero vector $X\in T_xM^n\,(x\in M)$, the angle $\theta(X)$ between $\varphi X$ and $T_xM^n$ is independent of the choice of $X\in T_xM$. In this case, $\theta$ defines a function on $M^n$, called the {\textit{slant function}}. In particular, if the slant function $\theta$ is a global constant on $M^{n}$, then $M^{n}$ is said to be a {\it slant submanifold} or a {\it $\theta$-slant submanifold}.
nodes.statement_short: A submanifold on which the angle between $\varphi X$ and the tangent space does not depend on $X$, giving a slant function $\theta$; constant $\theta$ gives a slant submanifold.
differentia: for any nonzero vector $X\in T_xM^n\,(x\in M)$, the angle $\theta(X)$ between $\varphi X$ and $T_xM^n$ is independent of the choice of $X\in T_xM$

nodes.name: Proper pointwise slant submanifold
nodes.statement: Anti-invariant submanifolds are slant submanifolds with slant function $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$. A pointwise slant submanifold is called {\it proper} if $0<\theta <\frac{\pi}{2}$.

nodes.name: Tangential and normal components $T, F, t, f$ of $\varphi$
nodes.statement: For any $X\in\Gamma(TM^n)$ and $N\in \Gamma(T^{\perp}M^n)$, we put $$\varphi X = T X + FX,\quad \varphi N = tN+fN,$$ where $TX$ (resp., $tN$) is the tangential component, and $FX$ (resp., $fN$) is the normal component of $\varphi X$ (resp. of $\varphi N$).

nodes.name: $CRS$ bi-warped product
nodes.statement: A {\it $CRS$ bi-warped product} of an almost contact metric manifold $(\widetilde M^{2m+1},g,\varphi,\xi,\eta)$ is a bi-warped product $M^n=N_{T}^{2p+1}\times_{f_1}N^{n_1}_\perp\times_{f_2}N^{n_2}_\theta$ in $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, where $N_{T}^{2p+1}$ is an invariant submanifold tangent to $\xi$, $N^{n_1}_\perp$ is an anti-invariant submanifold, $N^{n_2}_\theta$ is a pointwise slant submanifold of $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, and $f_{1}$ and $f_{2}$ are two positive smooth functions on $N_{T}^{2p+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: A bi-warped product whose three factors are respectively invariant (tangent to $\xi$), anti-invariant and pointwise slant submanifolds.
differentia: $N_{T}^{2p+1}$ is an invariant submanifold tangent to $\xi$
$N^{n_2}_\theta$ is a pointwise slant submanifold of $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$
$f_{1}$ and $f_{2}$ are two positive smooth functions on $N_{T}^{2p+1}$
nodes.section: Some basic results on $CRS$ bi-warped products

nodes.name: Contact CR-biwarped product
nodes.statement: A $CRS$ bi-warped product is a {\em{contact CR-biwarped product}} if it is of the form $M^n=N_{T}^{2p+1}\times_{f_1}N^{n_1}_\perp\times_{f_2}N^{n_2}_\perp$, where $N_{T}^{2p+1}$ is an invariant submanifold tangent to $\xi$, $N^{n_1}_\perp$ and $N^{n_2}_\perp$ are anti-invariant submanifolds of $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$.
differentia: $N^{n_1}_\perp$ and $N^{n_2}_\perp$ are anti-invariant submanifolds of $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$
nodes.section: Some basic results on $CRS$ bi-warped products

nodes.name: Dirichlet energy
nodes.statement: The Dirichlet energy of a function $\psi$ on a compact manifold $M$ is defined by \begin{align}E(\psi)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{M}\|\nabla\psi\|^2\,dV, \end{align} where $\nabla\psi$ is the gradient of $\psi$ and $dV$ is the volume element.
nodes.genus: functional of a function $\psi$ on a compact manifold $M$

nodes.name: Chen's non-existence of $N_{\perp}\times_{f} N_{T}$ warped products in Kaehler manifolds
nodes.statement: he proved in \cite{C3} that there do not exist warped products of the form $N_{\perp}\times_{f} N_{T}$ in any Kaehler manifold, where $N_{T}$ is a holomorphic submanifold and $N_{\perp}$ is a totally real submanifold.
nodes.statement_short: No Kaehler manifold admits a warped product with totally real base and holomorphic fibre.
assumptions: $N_{T}$ is a holomorphic submanifold and $N_{\perp}$ is a totally real submanifold
conclusions: there do not exist warped products of the form $N_{\perp}\times_{f} N_{T}$ in any Kaehler manifold

nodes.name: Chen's inequality for $CR$-warped products
nodes.statement: he proved that, for any warped product of the form $M=N_{T}\times_f N^{n_{1}}_{\perp}$ in any Kaehler manifold, the second fundamental form $h$ of $M$ satisfies $$||h||^2\geq 2n_1 ||\nabla(\ln f)||^2,$$ where $n_{1}=\dim\,N^{n_{1}}_{\perp}$ and $\nabla (\ln f)$ is the gradient of $\ln f$.
nodes.statement_short: For a $CR$-warped product in a Kaehler manifold the squared second fundamental form is at least $2n_1\|\nabla(\ln f)\|^2$.
assumptions: any warped product of the form $M=N_{T}\times_f N^{n_{1}}_{\perp}$ in any Kaehler manifold
$n_{1}=\dim\,N^{n_{1}}_{\perp}$ and $\nabla (\ln f)$ is the gradient of $\ln f$
conclusions: the second fundamental form $h$ of $M$ satisfies $||h||^2\geq 2n_1 ||\nabla(\ln f)||^2$

nodes.name: Theorem 5.2 (inequality for contact multiply CR-warped products)
nodes.statement: Let $M=N_T\times_{f_1}N_1^{n_{1}}\times\cdots\times_{f_k}N_k^{n_{k}}$ be a contact multiply CR-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. Then \begin{align} \|h\|^2\geq2\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_i \|\nabla(\ln f_i)\|^2. \end{align} The equality sign in \eqref{5.17} holds identically if and only if the following three conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] $N_T$ is a totally geodesic submanifold of $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. \item[(b)] $N_i\; (i=1,\cdots, k)$ are totally umbilical submanifolds of $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. \item[(c)] $_{f_1}N_1\times\cdots\times_{f_k}N_k$ is mixed totally geodesic in $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Extension of the CR-warped bound to $k$ anti-invariant factors, with a three-condition equality characterization.
assumptions: Let $M=N_T\times_{f_1}N_1^{n_{1}}\times\cdots\times_{f_k}N_k^{n_{k}}$ be a contact multiply CR-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$
conclusions: The equality sign in \eqref{5.17} holds identically if and only if the following three conditions hold: (a) $N_T$ is a totally geodesic submanifold of $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. (b) $N_i\; (i=1,\cdots, k)$ are totally umbilical submanifolds of $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. (c) $_{f_1}N_1\times\cdots\times_{f_k}N_k$ is mixed totally geodesic in $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$

nodes.name: Theorem 6.1 (Dirichlet energy inequality for the warping functions)
nodes.statement: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N^{n_1}_\perp\times_{f_2}N^{n_2}_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ with compact $N_T$. Then, for each $p\in N^{n_{1}}_\perp$ and $q\in N^{n_{2}}_\theta$, we have the following inequality for the Dirichlet energy of $f_1$ and $f_2$: \begin{equation}\begin{aligned}\notag n_1E(\ln f_1)+n_2(1+2\cot^{2}\theta)E(\ln f_2) \leq\frac{1}{4}\int_{N_T\times\{p\}\times\{q\}}\|h\|^2\,dV_T. \end{aligned}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Integrating the main inequality bounds a weighted sum of Dirichlet energies of $\ln f_1,\ln f_2$ by the total squared second fundamental form over $N_T$.
assumptions: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N^{n_1}_\perp\times_{f_2}N^{n_2}_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ with compact $N_T$
for each $p\in N^{n_{1}}_\perp$ and $q\in N^{n_{2}}_\theta$
conclusions: $n_1E(\ln f_1)+n_2(1+2\cot^{2}\theta)E(\ln f_2) \leq\frac{1}{4}\int_{N_T\times\{p\}\times\{q\}}\|h\|^2\,dV_T$

nodes.name: Characterization of Sasakian manifolds
nodes.statement: An almost contact metric manifold is Sasakian if and only if \begin{align} (\widetilde\nabla_X\varphi)Y=g(X, Y){\mathfrak{\xi}}-\eta(Y)X,\,\,\,\widetilde\nabla_X{\mathfrak{\xi}}=-\varphi X, \end{align} for any $X, Y\in\Gamma(T\widetilde M)$, where $\Gamma(T\widetilde M)$ is the Lie algebra of vector fields on $\widetilde M$.
assumptions: An almost contact metric manifold
for any $X, Y\in\Gamma(T\widetilde M)$, where $\Gamma(T\widetilde M)$ is the Lie algebra of vector fields on $\widetilde M$
conclusions: is Sasakian if and only if $(\widetilde\nabla_X\varphi)Y=g(X, Y){\mathfrak{\xi}}-\eta(Y)X,\,\,\,\widetilde\nabla_X{\mathfrak{\xi}}=-\varphi X$

nodes.name: Proposition 2.1 (characterization of pointwise slant submanifolds)
nodes.statement: Let $M^n$ be a submanifold of an almost contact metric manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ with $\mathfrak{\xi}\in\Gamma(TM^n)$. Then $M^n$ is pointwise slant if and only if \begin{align} T^2=\cos^2\theta\left(-I+\eta\otimes\mathfrak{\xi}\right),\end{align} where $\theta$ is the slant function and $I$ denotes the identity map on $TM^{n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise slantness is equivalent to the tensor identity $T^2=\cos^2\theta(-I+\eta\otimes\xi)$.
assumptions: Let $M^n$ be a submanifold of an almost contact metric manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ with $\mathfrak{\xi}\in\Gamma(TM^n)$
conclusions: $M^n$ is pointwise slant if and only if $T^2=\cos^2\theta\left(-I+\eta\otimes\mathfrak{\xi}\right)$, where $\theta$ is the slant function and $I$ denotes the identity map on $TM^{n}$

nodes.name: Proposition 2.2 (pointwise slant submanifolds of Sasakian manifolds)
nodes.statement: Every pointwise slant submanifold $M$ of a Sasakian manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ is anti-invariant if and only if the structure vector field $\xi$ is normal to $M$.
assumptions: Every pointwise slant submanifold $M$ of a Sasakian manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$
conclusions: is anti-invariant if and only if the structure vector field $\xi$ is normal to $M$

nodes.name: Proposition 3.1 (non-existence of $CRS$ bi-warped products in Sasakian manifolds)
nodes.statement: There do not exist $CRS$ bi-warped products in a Sasakian manifold other than contact $CR$-biwarped products.
conclusions: There do not exist $CRS$ bi-warped products in a Sasakian manifold other than contact $CR$-biwarped products
nodes.section: Some basic results on $CRS$ bi-warped products

nodes.name: Proposition 4.1 (constancy of $f_1$ versus mixed total geodesy)
nodes.statement: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ such that $h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)\perp\mu$. Then the warping function $f_1$ is constant if and only if $M^n$ is ${\mathfrak{D}^{T}}\oplus{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp$-mixed totally geodesic in $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, i.e., $h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)=\{0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Under $h(\mathfrak D^T,\mathfrak D^\perp)\perp\mu$, $f_1$ is constant exactly when $M$ is $\mathfrak D^T\oplus\mathfrak D^\perp$-mixed totally geodesic.
assumptions: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ such that $h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)\perp\mu$
conclusions: the warping function $f_1$ is constant if and only if $M^n$ is ${\mathfrak{D}^{T}}\oplus{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp$-mixed totally geodesic in $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, i.e., $h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)=\{0\}$

nodes.name: Proposition 4.2 (constancy of $f_2$ versus mixed total geodesy)
nodes.statement: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ such that $h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)\perp\mu$. Then $f_2$ is constant on $M$ if and only if $M^n$ is ${\mathfrak{D}^{T}}\oplus{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta$-mixed totally geodesic in $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Under $h(\mathfrak D^T,\mathfrak D^\theta)\perp\mu$, $f_2$ is constant exactly when $M$ is $\mathfrak D^T\oplus\mathfrak D^\theta$-mixed totally geodesic.
assumptions: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ such that $h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)\perp\mu$
conclusions: $f_2$ is constant on $M$ if and only if $M^n$ is ${\mathfrak{D}^{T}}\oplus{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta$-mixed totally geodesic in $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 ($\xi$-derivatives of the warping functions vanish)
nodes.statement: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. Then $\xi(\ln f_1)=\xi(\ln f_2)=0$ and $h(X, \xi)=0$ for every $X\in \Gamma(N_{\perp}\times N_{\theta})$.
assumptions: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$
conclusions: $h(X, \xi)=0$ for every $X\in \Gamma(N_{\perp}\times N_{\theta})$

nodes.name: Lemma 4.2 (components of the second fundamental form)
nodes.statement: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. Then we have \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] $g(h(X, Y), \varphi Z)=0=g(h(X, Y),FV)$; \item [(ii)] $g(h(X, Z), \varphi W)=-\varphi X(\ln f_1)\,g(Z, W)$; \item[(iii)] $g(h(X,U), FV)=-\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V)-X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV)$. \end{enumerate} for $X,Y\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}^{T}})$, $Z,W\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)$ and $U,V\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Computes the $\varphi\mathfrak D^\perp$- and $F\mathfrak D^\theta$-components of $h$ on the three distributions in terms of derivatives of $\ln f_1,\ln f_2$.
assumptions: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$
for $X,Y\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}^{T}})$, $Z,W\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)$ and $U,V\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)$
conclusions: $g(h(X, Y), \varphi Z)=0=g(h(X, Y),FV)$
$g(h(X, Z), \varphi W)=-\varphi X(\ln f_1)\,g(Z, W)$
$g(h(X,U), FV)=-\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V)-X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV)$

nodes.name: Lemma 4.3 (mixed components vanish)
nodes.statement: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. Then \begin{align} g(h(X, Z),FV)=g(h(X, V), \varphi Z)=0,\end{align} for any $X\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}^{T}})$, $Z\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)$ and $V\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)$.
assumptions: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$
for any $X\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}^{T}})$, $Z\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)$ and $V\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)$
conclusions: $g(h(X, Z),FV)=g(h(X, V), \varphi Z)=0$

nodes.name: Corollary 3.1 (no proper pointwise semi-slant warped products in Sasakian manifolds)
nodes.statement: There do not exist any proper pointwise semi-slant warped product submanifold $M=N_T\times_fN_\theta$ in a Sasakian manifold.
conclusions: There do not exist any proper pointwise semi-slant warped product submanifold $M=N_T\times_fN_\theta$ in a Sasakian manifold

nodes.statement: Let $M=N_T\times_fN^{n_{1}}_\perp$ be a contact CR-warped product of a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. If $N_T$ is compact and $q\in N^{n_{1}}_\perp$, then \begin{align}\notag E(\ln f_1)\le\frac{1}{4n_1}\int_{N_T\times\{q\}}\|h\|^2\,dV_T. \end{align}
assumptions: Let $M=N_T\times_fN^{n_{1}}_\perp$ be a contact CR-warped product of a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$
If $N_T$ is compact and $q\in N^{n_{1}}_\perp$
conclusions: $E(\ln f_1)\le\frac{1}{4n_1}\int_{N_T\times\{q\}}\|h\|^2\,dV_T$

nodes.name: Corollary 6.2 (Dirichlet energy bound for pointwise semi-slant warped products)
nodes.statement: Let $M=N_T\times_fN^{n_{2}}_\theta$ be a pointwise semi-slant warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$. If $N_T$ is compact and $s\in N^{n_{2}}_\theta$, then \begin{align}\notag E(\ln f_2)\le\frac{1}{4n_2(1+2\cot^2\theta)}\int_{N_T\times\{s\}}\|h\|^2\,dV_T. \end{align}
assumptions: Let $M=N_T\times_fN^{n_{2}}_\theta$ be a pointwise semi-slant warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$
If $N_T$ is compact and $s\in N^{n_{2}}_\theta$
conclusions: $E(\ln f_2)\le\frac{1}{4n_2(1+2\cot^2\theta)}\int_{N_T\times\{s\}}\|h\|^2\,dV_T$

nodes.name: Remark 3.1 (base totally geodesic, fibre totally umbilical)
nodes.statement: It is well known that, for a warped product manifold $M=B\times_fF$ , $B$ is totally geodesic and $F$ is totally umbilical in $M$ (see, e.g., \cite{C3,oneill}).

nodes.name: Remark 3.2 (totally geodesic factors of a $CRS$ bi-warped product)
nodes.statement: It follows from Remark \ref{R:3.1} that $N_{T}, N_{T}\times_{f_1}N^{n_1}_\perp$ and $N_{T}\times_{f_2}N^{n_2}_\theta$ are totally geodesic in the $CRS$ bi-warped product $M^n=N_{T}\times_{f_1}N^{n_1}_\perp\times_{f_2}N^{n_2}_\theta$.

nodes.name: Remark on other positions of the characteristic vector field
nodes.statement: One may also prove that there are no proper bi-warped products of the form $M=N_{T}\times_{f_{1}} N_{\perp}\times_{f_{2}} N_{\theta}$ in a Sasakian manifold such that the characteristic vector field $\xi$ is tangent to either $N_{\perp}$ or to $N_{\theta}$, or $\xi$ is normal to $M$.
nodes.section: Some basic results on $CRS$ bi-warped products

nodes.name: Remark on the extension to contact multiply CR-warped products
nodes.statement: By applying the same methods given in \cite{CD} and in \cite{HM}, we have the following extension of Corollary \ref{C:5.1} to contact multiply CR-warped product $N_T\times_{f_1}N_1^{n_{1}}\times\cdots\times_{f_k}N_k^{n_{k}}$ of cosymplectic manifolds $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, where $N_T$ is invariant and $N_{1}^{1},\ldots,N_{k}^{n_{k}}$ are anti-invariant submanifolds of $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$.
nodes.section: A general inequality for bi-warped products

nodes.name: Gauss and Weingarten formulas
nodes.statement:
Let $M^n$ be an $n$-dimensional submanifold of an almost contact metric manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ such that the structure vector field ${\mathfrak{\xi}}$ tangent to $M^n$ with induced metric $g$. Let $\Gamma(T^\perp M^{n})$ denote the space of all vector fields normal to $M^n$. Then the Gauss and Weingarten formulas are given respectively by (see, e,g., \cite{book11,book17, Ya})  egin{equation} egin{aligned} \widetilde
abla_XY=
abla_XY+h(X, Y), \quad \widetilde
abla_XN=-A_NX+
abla^{\perp}_XN, \end{aligned}\end{equation} for $X, Y\in\Gamma(TM^n)$ and $N\in\Gamma(T^{\perp}M^{n})$, where $
abla$ and $
abla^{\perp}$ denote the connections on the tangent and normal bundles of $M^n$, respectively, and $A$ the shape operator of $M^n$. It is well known that the second fundamental form $h$ and the shape operator $A$ are related by $g(h(X, Y), N)=g(A_NX, Y).$
nodes.statement_short: The Gauss and Weingarten decompositions of the ambient connection, and the duality $g(h(X,Y),N)=g(A_NX,Y)$.

nodes.name: Components of the second fundamental form and $\|h\|^2$
nodes.statement: Let $x\in M^n$ and $e_1,\cdots, e_n, e_{n+1},\cdots, e_{2m+1}$ are orthonormal basis of the tangent space $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ such that restricted to $M^n$, $e_1,\cdots, e_n$ are tangent to $M^n$ and hence $e_{n+1},\cdots, e_{2m+1}$ are normal to $M^n$. Let $\{h^r_{ij}\}\,(1\leq i, j\leq n;\,n+1\leq r\leq 2m+1)$ denote the coefficients of $h$ with respect to the local frame field. Then \begin{align} h_{ij}^r=g(h(e_i, e_j), e_r)=g(A_{e_r}e_i, e_j),\,\,\,\|h\|^2=\sum_{i,j=1}^ng(h(e_i, e_j), h(e_i, e_j)).\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Definition of the frame coefficients $h^r_{ij}$ and of the squared norm $\|h\|^2$.

nodes.name: Metric relations for $T$ and $F$ on pointwise slant submanifolds
nodes.statement: Following relations are straightforward consequence of \eqref{charac} \begin{align} &g(TX,TY)=\cos^2\theta[g(X,Y)-\eta(X)\eta(Y)], \\ &g(FX, FY) =\sin^2\theta[g(X, Y)-\eta(X)\eta(Y)], \end{align} for vector fields $X,Y\in \Gamma(M^n)$.

nodes.name: Relations for $tF$ and $fF$ on pointwise slant submanifolds
nodes.statement: Also, for pointwise slant submanifolds, we have \begin{align} tFX=\sin^2\theta\left(-X+\eta(X)\mathfrak{\xi}\right),~~~~fFX=-FTX,\quad X\in\Gamma(TM^n). \end{align}

nodes.name: Levi-Civita connection of a bi-warped product
nodes.statement:
Let $M=B	imes_{f_1}N$ with $N=N_1	imes_{f_2}N_2$ be a bi-warped product submanifold of a Riemannian manifold $\widetilde M$. Put ${\mathfrak{D}}=TB$. Then we have  egin{align} 
abla_ZX= 
abla_XZ=\sum_{i=1}^2X(\ln f_i) Z^i \end{align} for any $X\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}})$ and $Z\in\Gamma(TN)$, where $Z^i$ denotes the $N_i$-component of $Z$, and $
abla$ is the Levi-Civita connection on $M$ (see, e.g., \cite{UFH}).
nodes.statement_short: Mixed covariant derivatives on a bi-warped product are given by the logarithmic warping derivatives $X(\ln f_i)$.
nodes.section: Some basic results on $CRS$ bi-warped products

nodes.name: Tangent and normal space decomposition of a $CRS$ bi-warped product
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak{D}^{T}},\,\,{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp$ and ${\mathfrak{D}}^\theta$ denote the tangent bundles of $N_T,\,\,N_\perp$ and $N_\theta$, respectively. Then the tangent and normal spaces of $M^n$ are given respectively by \begin{align} & TM^n={\mathfrak{D}^{T}}\oplus{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp\oplus{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta, \quad T^\perp M^n=\varphi{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp\oplus F{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta\oplus\mu, \end{align} where $\mu$ is the invariant subbundle of $T^\perp M^n$. Clearly, ${\rm Span}\{\xi\}\subset {\mathfrak{D}^{T}}$ by definition.
nodes.statement_short: $TM^n$ splits as $\mathfrak D^T\oplus\mathfrak D^\perp\oplus\mathfrak D^\theta$ and $T^\perp M^n$ as $\varphi\mathfrak D^\perp\oplus F\mathfrak D^\theta\oplus\mu$.
nodes.section: Some basic results on $CRS$ bi-warped products

nodes.name: Relation obtained by replacing $X$ by $\varphi X$ in Lemma 4.2(ii)
nodes.statement: Replacing $X$ by $\varphi X$ in Lemma \ref{L:4.2}(ii) and using \eqref{struc} and Lemma \ref{L:4.1}, we find \begin{align} g(h(\varphi X, Z), \varphi W)=X(\ln f_1)g(Z, W). \end{align}

nodes.name: Seven useful relations for the slant components of $h$
nodes.statement: Similarly, if we replace $X$ by $\varphi X$, $U$ by $TU$, and $V$ by $TV$ in Lemma \ref{L:4.2}(iii), we obtain the following useful relations: \begin{align} &g(h(\varphi X, U), FV)=X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V)-\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV), \\ &g(h(X,TU), FV)=\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV)-\cos^2\theta\,X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V), \\ & g(h(X,U), FTV)=\cos^2\theta\,X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V)-\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV), \\& g(h(\varphi X,TU), FV)=-X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV)-\cos^2\theta\,\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V), \\& g(h(\varphi X, U), FTV)=X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV)+\cos^2\theta\,\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V), \\ &g(h(X, TU), FTV)=-\cos^2\theta\,X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV)-\cos^2\theta\,\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V), \\& g(h(\varphi X, TU), FTV)=\cos^2\theta\,X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V)-\cos^2\theta\,\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Seven substitution identities expressing $g(h(\cdot,\cdot),F\cdot)$ in terms of $X(\ln f_2)$, $\varphi X(\ln f_2)$ and $\cos^2\theta$.

nodes.name: Adapted orthonormal frames for $\mathfrak{D}^{T},\mathfrak{D}^\perp,\mathfrak{D}^\theta,\varphi\mathfrak{D}^\perp,F\mathfrak{D}^\theta$ and $\mu$
nodes.statement: Let $M^n=N_T\times_{f_1}N^{n_{1}}_\perp\times_{f_2}N^{n_{2}}_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ with $\dim N_{T}=2p+1$. We choose orthonormal frames of ${\mathfrak{D}^{T}},\, {\mathfrak{D}}^\perp$ and ${\mathfrak{D}}^\theta$ of $TM^n$ given respectively by \begin{align*} &{\mathfrak{D}^{T}}=\rm{Span}\{e_1,\,\cdots,e_{p},\,e_{p+1}=\varphi e_{1},\,\cdots,e_{2p}=\varphi e_{p}, e_{2p+1}={\mathfrak{\xi}}\},\;\\&{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp=\rm{Span}\{e_{2p+2}=\bar e_1,\,\cdots,\,e_{2p+1+n_1}=\bar e_{n_1}\},\\ &{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta=\rm{Span}\{e_{2p+2+n_1}=e_1^{*},\,\cdots,\,e_{2p+1+n_1+s}=e_s^{*},\,\\&\hskip.5in e_{2p+2+n_1+s}=e_{s+1}^{*}=\sec\theta\, Te_1^{*},\cdots, e_{n}=e_{2s}^{*}=\sec\theta\, Te_{s}^{*}\}. \end{align*} Then we have the following orthonormal frames for $\varphi{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp,\,F\mathfrak{D}^\theta$ and $\mu$ as follows: \begin{align*} &\varphi{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp=\rm{Span}\{e_{n+1}= \varphi\bar e_1,\cdots,\, e_{n+n_1}=\varphi\bar e_{n_1}\},\\ &F\mathfrak{D}^\theta=\rm{Span}\{e_{n+n_1+1}=\hat{e}_{1}=\csc\theta\, Fe_{1}^{*},\cdots,\,e_{n+n_1+s}=\hat{e}_{s}=\csc\theta\, Fe_{s}^{*},\\ &\hskip.2in e_{n+n_1+s+1}=\hat{e}_{s+1}=\csc\theta\sec\theta\, FTe_{1}^{*},\cdots,\, e_{n+n_1+n_2}=\hat{e}_{n_2}=\csc\theta\sec\theta\, FTe_{s}^{*}\},\\ &\mu=\rm{Span}\{e_{n+n_1+n_2+1}=\widetilde e_{1},\cdots, e_{2m+1}=\widetilde e_{2m+1-n-n_1-n_2}\}. \end{align*} Clearly, ${\rm rank}\;{\varphi\mathfrak{D}}^\perp=n_1,\,\,{\rm rank}\; F{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta=2s=n_2$ and ${\rm rank}\;\mu=2m+1-n-n_1-n_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Choice of adapted orthonormal frames on the three tangent distributions and the three normal subbundles, with their ranks.

nodes.name: Standing assumption: $\xi$ tangent to $N_T$ in a cosymplectic ambient manifold
nodes.statement: From now on, assume that $M=N_{T}\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ is a $CRS$ bi-warped product of a cosymplectic manifold $\widetilde M$ whose structure vector field $\xi$ is tangent to $N_T$.

nodes.statement: In order to do so, we assume that the invariant factor $N_{T}$ of the $CRS$ bi-warped product is compact without boundary.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: From \eqref{sasaki} and \eqref{gauss}, we have \begin{align} A_\mathfrak{\xi}X=TX,\quad \nabla^\perp_X\xi=-FX, \end{align} for any $X\in\Gamma(TM)$. Taking the inner product in \eqref{cs1} with $Y\in\Gamma(TM)$, we get \begin{align} g(h(X, Y), \mathfrak{\xi})=g(TX, Y). \end{align} From \eqref{cs2}, we find $\cos^2\theta\;g(X, Y)=0$ via polarization identity. Since, the metric $g$ is Riemannian, we obtain $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$. The converse is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the Sasakian identity with the Gauss/Weingarten formulas, polarize $g(h(X,Y),\xi)=g(TX,Y)$, and conclude $\theta=\pi/2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement: Let $M=N_{T}\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a Sasakian manifold $\widetilde M$. If $V\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)$, it follows from \e{struc}, \e{sasaki}, \e{gauss} and \e{warped} that \begin{align}\xi(\ln f_{2})V+ h(\xi,V)=\nabla_{V}\xi +h(\xi,V)=\widetilde \nabla_{V}\xi=-\varphi V=- TV -FV.\end{align} By comparing the tangential components of \e{3.04}, we find $\xi(\ln f_{2})V=-TV$, which implies $\xi(\ln f_{2})=0$ and $TV=0$. Hence, we find $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Consequently, $M$ is a contact $CR$-biwarped product.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate $\xi$ along a slant vector, compare tangential components to force $TV=0$, hence $\theta=\pi/2$.
nodes.section: Some basic results on $CRS$ bi-warped products

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement:
It follows from \e{gauss} and \e{cosy} that $
abla_{X}\xi+h(X,\xi)=\widetilde 
abla_X {\xi}=0$ for every $X\in \Gamma(N_{\perp}	imes N_{	heta})$, which implies $
abla_{X}\xi=0$ and $h(X,\xi)=0$. Now, after combining $
abla_{X}\xi=0$ with \e{warped}, we obtain $\xi(\ln f_1)=\xi(\ln f_2)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\widetilde\nabla\xi=0$ in the Gauss formula to split off $\nabla_X\xi=0$ and $h(X,\xi)=0$, then apply the warped connection formula.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement:
For any $X, Y\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}^{T}})$ and $Z\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)$, we find  egin{align*} g(h(X, Y), \varphi Z)\, &=g(\widetilde
abla_XY, \varphi Z)=-g(\widetilde
abla_X\varphi Y, Z)=-g(
abla_X\varphi Y, Z). \end{align*} Using the fact that $N_T$ is totally geodesic in $M^n$ (see Remark ef{R:3.1}) with the orthogonality of vector fields, we find $g(h(X, Y), \varphi Z)=0$, which is the first equality of (i). Similarly, we have the second equality of (i). For (ii), we have  egin{align*} g(h(X, Z), \varphi W)\, &=g(\widetilde
abla_ZX, \varphi W)=g((\widetilde
abla_Z\varphi)X, W)-g((\widetilde
abla_Z\varphi X, W). \end{align*} Using \eqref{cosy}, Remark ef{R:3.2}, and \eqref{warped} with the orthogonality of vector fields, we get (ii). Similarly, we obtain (iii).
nodes.statement_short: Move $\varphi$ across the metric using $\widetilde\nabla\varphi=0$, then use total geodesy of $N_T$ and the warped connection formula for each of the three parts.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement_short: Expand each mixed component with the Gauss and warped-connection formulas; orthogonality of the distributions kills both terms.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.1
nodes.statement: If $M^n$ is ${\mathfrak{D}^{T}}\oplus{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp$-mixed totally geodesic, \eqref{4.2} implies that $f_1$ is constant. Conversely, if $f_1$ is constant, then it follows from Lemma \ref{L:4.3} that \begin{align} g(h(\mathfrak{D}^{T}, \mathfrak{D}^\perp),F\mathfrak{D}^\theta)=0. \end{align} On the other hand, we find from \eqref{4.2} that $g(h(\mathfrak{D}^{T}, \mathfrak{D}^\perp), \varphi \mathfrak{D}^\perp)=0.$ Also, from the hypothesis of the proposition we have $g(h(\mathfrak{D}^{T}, \mathfrak{D}^\perp), \mu)=0.$ Thus, we get $g(h(\mathfrak{D}^{T}, \mathfrak{D}^\perp), N)=0$ for any $N\in\Gamma(T^\perp M^n)$. Therefore, $M^n$ is $\mathfrak{D}^{T}\oplus\mathfrak{D}^\perp$-mixed totally geodesic.
nodes.statement_short: Two-directional argument: mixed total geodesy forces $f_1$ constant, and conversely all three normal components of $h(\mathfrak D^T,\mathfrak D^\perp)$ vanish.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.2
nodes.statement: If $M^n$ is ${\mathfrak{D}^{T}}\oplus{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta$-mixed totally geodesic, then \eqref{4.2} yields \begin{align} X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V)=\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV). \end{align} Also, from \eqref{4.3} we find $\varphi X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, TV)=\cos^2\theta\,X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V)$. Combining this with \eqref{4.13} gives $\sin^2\theta\,X(\ln f_2)\,g(U, V)=0$. Because $g$ is Riemannian metric, this implies that $\sin^2\theta\, X(\ln f_2)=0.$ Since $N_\theta$ is proper pointwise slant, we must have $X(\ln f_2)=0$. Thus $f_2$ is constant. Conversely, if $f_2$ is constant, then \eqref{4.2} gives $g(h(\mathfrak{D}^{T}, \mathfrak{D}^\theta),F\mathfrak{D}^\theta)=0$. Further, it follows from the second equality of Lemma \ref{L:4.3} that $g(h(\mathfrak{D}^{T}, \mathfrak{D}^\theta), \varphi \mathfrak{D}^\perp)=0.$ Moreover, we find from the hypothesis that $g(h(\mathfrak{D}^{T}, \mathfrak{D}^\theta), \mu)=0$. Consequently, $M^n$ is ${\mathfrak{D}^{T}}\oplus\mathfrak{D}^\theta$-mixed totally geodesic.
nodes.statement_short: Combine two of the substitution identities to get $\sin^2\theta\,X(\ln f_2)=0$, then run the converse through the three normal components.

nodes.name: Derive the shape operator and normal connection along $\xi$
nodes.statement: From \eqref{sasaki} and \eqref{gauss}, we have \begin{align} A_\mathfrak{\xi}X=TX,\quad \nabla^\perp_X\xi=-FX, \end{align} for any $X\in\Gamma(TM)$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up $A_\xi X=TX$ and $\nabla^\perp_X\xi=-FX$ from the Sasakian and Gauss/Weingarten formulas.

nodes.name: Take the inner product with $Y$
nodes.statement: Taking the inner product in \eqref{cs1} with $Y\in\Gamma(TM)$, we get \begin{align} g(h(X, Y), \mathfrak{\xi})=g(TX, Y). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Pair the previous identity with a tangent field to get $g(h(X,Y),\xi)=g(TX,Y)$.

nodes.name: Polarize and conclude $\theta=\pi/2$
nodes.statement: From \eqref{cs2}, we find $\cos^2\theta\;g(X, Y)=0$ via polarization identity. Since, the metric $g$ is Riemannian, we obtain $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$. The converse is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Polarization gives $\cos^2\theta\,g=0$, so $\theta=\pi/2$; the converse is immediate.

nodes.name: Set up a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a Sasakian manifold
nodes.statement: Let $M=N_{T}\times_{f_1}N_\perp\times_{f_2}N_\theta$ be a $CRS$ bi-warped product in a Sasakian manifold $\widetilde M$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the ambient Sasakian setting.

nodes.name: Compute $\widetilde\nabla_V\xi$ for a slant vector field
nodes.statement: If $V\in \Gamma({\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)$, it follows from \e{struc}, \e{sasaki}, \e{gauss} and \e{warped} that \begin{align}\xi(\ln f_{2})V+ h(\xi,V)=\nabla_{V}\xi +h(\xi,V)=\widetilde \nabla_{V}\xi=-\varphi V=- TV -FV.\end{align}

nodes.name: Compare tangential components and conclude
nodes.statement: By comparing the tangential components of \e{3.04}, we find $\xi(\ln f_{2})V=-TV$, which implies $\xi(\ln f_{2})=0$ and $TV=0$. Hence, we find $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Consequently, $M$ is a contact $CR$-biwarped product.

nodes.name: Discard the unusable non-negative terms
nodes.statement: Let us omit the positive 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th, 15th and 18th terms of $\mu$-components in the right hand side of \eqref{5.2}. Since we couldn't find any relations for the 4th, 5th, 7th, 8th, 16th and 17th terms, we also omit these positive terms and using Lemma \ref{L:4.2}(i), the 1st and 2nd terms vanish identically. Similarly, the 11th and 13th terms vanish according to Lemma \ref{L:4.3}. Hence, with the remaining 10th and 14th terms, the above expression becomes \begin{equation}\begin{aligned} \|h\|^2\geq\; & 2\sum_{r=1}^{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{p}\sum_{j=1}^{n_1}g(h(e_i, \bar e_j), \varphi \bar e_r)^2+2\sum_{r=1}^{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{p}\sum_{j=1}^{n_1}g(h(\varphi e_i, \bar e_j), \varphi \bar e_r)^2\\ &+2\sum_{r=1}^{n_1}\sum_{j=1}^{n_1}g(h(\mathfrak{\xi}, \bar e_j), \varphi \bar e_r)^2+2\sum_{r=1}^{n_2}\sum_{i=1}^{p}\sum_{j=1}^{n_2}g(h(e_i, e_j^{*}), \hat e_r)^2 \\& +2\sum_{r=1}^{n_2}\sum_{i=1}^{p}\sum_{j=1}^{n_2}g(h(\varphi e_i, e_j^{*}), \hat e_r)^2+2\sum_{r=1}^{n_2}\sum_{j=1}^{n_2}g(h((\mathfrak{\xi}, e_j^{*}), \hat e_r)^2. \end{aligned}\end{equation}

Then, by using (ii)-(iii) of Lemma \ref{L:4.2} and \eqref{4.2}-\eqref{4.8} with orthonormality of vector fields, we find \begin{align} \|h\|^2\; & \geq2n_1\sum_{i=1}^{p}(e_i\ln f_1)^2+2n_1\sum_{i=1}^{p}(\varphi e_i\ln f_1)^2+2n_2(\csc^2\theta+\cot^2\theta)\sum_{i=1}^{p}(\varphi e_i\ln f_2)^2\notag\\ &+2n_2(\csc^2\theta+\cot^2\theta)\sum_{i=1}^{p}(e_i\ln f_2)^2. \end{align}

nodes.statement: Since $\mathfrak{\xi}(\ln f_1)=\mathfrak{\xi}(\ln f_2)=0$ from Lemma \ref{L:4.1}, the above relation becomes \begin{equation}\begin{aligned} \|h\|^2&\geq2n_1\sum_{i=1}^{2p+1}(e_i\ln f_1)^2+2n_2(\csc^2\theta+\cot^2\theta)\sum_{i=1}^{2p+1}(e_i\ln f_2). \end{aligned}\end{equation} So, we find the inequality given in statement (i) via the definition of gradient.

nodes.name: Equality: $h(TM,TM)\perp\mu$ and $h(\mathfrak{D}^\perp,\mathfrak{D}^\perp)=\{0\}$
nodes.statement: For the equality, it follows from the omitted $\mu$-components terms in \eqref{5.2} that\begin{align} h(TM, TM)\perp\mu \end{align} Also, from the omitted 4th and 5th terms in \eqref{5.2}, we have \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp, {\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)\perp \varphi{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp,\,\,\,\,\,h({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp, {\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)\perp F{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta. \end{align} Then we obtain from \eqref{eq1} and \eqref{eq2} that \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp, {\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)=\{0\}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Equality forces the discarded terms to vanish, giving $h\perp\mu$ and $h(\mathfrak D^\perp,\mathfrak D^\perp)=\{0\}$.

nodes.name: Equality: $h(\mathfrak{D}^\theta,\mathfrak{D}^\theta)=\{0\}$
nodes.statement: From the omitted 7th and 8th terms in the right hand side of \eqref{5.2}, we get \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}}^\theta, {\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)\perp \varphi{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp,\,\,\,\,\,h({\mathfrak{D}}^\theta, {\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)\perp F{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta. \end{align} Thus we conclude from \eqref{eq1} and \eqref{eq5} that \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}}^\theta, {\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)=\{0\}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Equality: $h(\mathfrak{D}^\perp,\mathfrak{D}^\theta)=\{0\}$
nodes.statement: Similarly, from the omitted 16th and 17th terms in the right hand side of \eqref{5.2}, we arrive at \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp, {\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)\perp\varphi{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp,\,\,\,\,\,h({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp, {\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)\perp F{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta. \end{align} From \eqref{eq1} and \eqref{eq7}, we find \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}}^\perp, {\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)=\{0\}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The mixed anti-invariant/slant terms vanish, so $h(\mathfrak D^\perp,\mathfrak D^\theta)=\{0\}$.

nodes.name: Equality: $h(\mathfrak{D}^{T},\mathfrak{D}^{T})=\{0\}$ and the two inclusions
nodes.statement: On the other hand, we find from the vanishing 1st and 2nd terms of \e{5.2} that \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}^{T}})\perp\varphi{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp,\,\,\,\,\,h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}},\, {\mathfrak{D}^{T}})\perp F{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta. \end{align} Thus, we derive from \eqref{eq1} and \eqref{eq9}, that \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}^{T}})=\{0\}. \end{align} And, from the vanishing 11th term of \eqref{5.2} and \eqref{eq1}, we get \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}}^\perp)\subset \varphi{\mathfrak{D}}^\perp. \end{align} Similarly, from the vanishing 13th term in \eqref{5.2} with \eqref{eq1}, we find \begin{align} h({\mathfrak{D}^{T}}, {\mathfrak{D}}^\theta)\subset F{\mathfrak{D}}^\theta. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The invariant-block terms vanish too, and the two surviving mixed blocks land in $\varphi\mathfrak D^\perp$ and $F\mathfrak D^\theta$.
